remaining_uncertainties: No citation chasing was possible (Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex returned HTTP 429), so 'no paper found' cannot be read as 'no paper exists' for the surviving candidate.
The surviving candidate C1 depends on an unverified premise: that task pairs with equal difficulty but different spatial tolerance can be constructed. No pilot evidence exists.
43 of 88 registered papers were read at abstract level only (arXiv HTML rate limits); they may contain direct competitors that would change the crowding judgement.
Conference-versus-arXiv version differences were not compared, and venue status could not be verified for most 2026 preprints.
Real-robot evidence throughout the field is based on 20-30 trials per condition, which limits the statistical strength of any action-level claim, including future ones.
Whether a measurement/prediction contribution is acceptable as the master's small paper is a taste/advisor judgement that literature research cannot settle.
conclusion: Across 130 queries and 88 registered papers, five of seven screened directions (cross-view consistency, 3D representation upgrades, active re-observation, spatial-interface design, phase-localised grounding diagnosis) fail the hard vetoes because multiple 2024-2026 papers already solve them or the increment can be obtained by a simple modification. Only one candidate survives: C1, whether task action tolerance plus baseline shortcut reliance and effective spatial-error reduction can predict the action benefit of a spatial representation upgrade. It survives as a measurement-and-prediction question, not as a new module, and it is conditional on constructing same-difficulty/different-tolerance task pairs and on first establishing a reliable baseline. The report therefore recommends no experiment until four explicit gates are met.
